page.layout: Running head and page number at the top. Below them a printed ornament. Then a centred title block, theses, problem heading and question, all at full width. Below that one text column with marginal notes in the left margin, beginning with "Thesis affirm. defenditur." and "Ratio" beside the first paragraph, then I., II., III. beside its lines, and "Obiectio." beside the second paragraph. No catchword or signature.

main_text.head: METAPHYSICÆ LIBER QUARTUS; De Substantiis.
De substantia in genere, Cap. I.
THEOREMATA.

p.i: 1 Hactenus explicata est prima, nempe Universalis pars Metaphysica. Sequitur altera, nempe Particularis, qua agit de ente incomplexo in specie.
2 Eius duae sunt partes: Una, de Substantiis; altera de Accidentibus.
3 Ens enim incomplexum aut est substantia, aut accidens.
4 Substantia est ens incomplexum, per se subsistens.

main_text.head: IN CAPUT PRIMUM
PROBLEMA I.

head.i: Utrum tractatio speciālis de ente incomplexo pertineat ad Metaphysicam?

main_text.p: Thesis affirm. defenditur.RatioSTatuitur sententia affirmativa. Rationes sunt: 1, Quia tractatio specialis de ente incomplexo sub ratione formalem subiecti Metaphysicæ cadit, neque I.eius terminos transgreditur: Siquidem in ea consideratur ens incomplexum, quatenus sine ullo materiæ conceptu est intelligibile. 2, Quia Metaphysica est ars ca-II.tholica seu universalis: Ideoque officium eius est explicare doctrinam generalem de substantiis & accidentibus, utpote cuius usus per omnia reliquarum disciplina-III.rum genera latissime est diffusus. 3, Quia omnes Philosophi, qui unquam Metaphysicam conscripserunt, aut de rebus Metaphysicis differuerunt, in eo semper consenserunt, esse in illa disciplina de ente incomplexo in specie agendum: Ideoque cum artificibus in sua arte sit credendum, sequitur tractationem specialem de ente incomplexo ex Metaphysicæ finibus non esse eiiciendam.
Obiectio.Verum contra hanc sententiam obiici possunt duo potiffi.[?]

page.notes: The printed word "Virum" in the problem title is read as "Utrum" under the u/v rule. The final word "potiffi." is read with [?] and may be an abbreviation or a worn letter. The large initial "S" of the first paragraph is joined to the word as "STatuitur". Notes I., II., III. are placed at the approximate line where they stand; their exact position within the line is uncertain. The top right corner has a blurred shape and the bottom right shows a faint mark; these are not printed text and are left out.
